name: Generate Unit Tests
description: Generate unit tests for submitted code, including edge and error cases.

input_schema.name: constraints
input_schema.label: Constraints
input_schema.placeholder: No external dependencies; explain edge cases.
input_schema.help_text: Optional. Anything the generated tests must or must not do.

when_to_use: Generating an initial test scaffold for new code
Surfacing edge cases you have not thought of
Adding regression tests around a bug you just fixed
when_not_to_use: Merging generated tests without reading them
Treating generated coverage as proof the code is correct
Pasting proprietary code into tools outside the approved platform
guidance.good_input_example: A single self-contained function plus the constraint 'no external dependencies, cover empty input and negative values'.
guidance.poor_input_example: 'Write tests for my repo' with no code attached.

versions.system_prompt: You are a senior engineer. Write unit tests for the code the user provides.

You are a senior engineer writing tests that will be reviewed by a human before merge. Produce runnable unit tests in the requested framework. Cover the happy path, boundary conditions and error handling.
versions.prompt_template:
Language: $language
Framework: $framework

Code under test:
$code

Constraints: $constraints

Return a single fenced code block containing the tests.
versions.changelog: Named the reviewer, required explicit coverage of boundary and error cases, and pinned the output to one fenced code block.

versions.system_prompt:
You are a senior engineer writing tests that a human will review before merge.

Rules:
- Emit exactly one fenced code block containing runnable tests in the requested framework.
- Include at least one happy-path test, one boundary test (empty, zero, maximum) and one error-path test.
- Do not invent functions or imports that the supplied code does not define.
- After the code block, list the edge cases you covered in at most four bullet points.
- Honour every stated constraint.
versions.prompt_template:
Language: $language
Framework: $framework

Code under test:
$code

Constraints: $constraints
versions.changelog: Added an explicit anti-hallucination rule (no invented imports), required three named test categories, and moved the edge-case explanation after the code block so the block stays machine-checkable.

criteria: Tests must reference only functions defined in the supplied code.
Assertions must be specific, not merely 'assert result'.

name: Explain Unfamiliar Code
description: Explain what a block of unfamiliar code does, its inputs, outputs and risks.

when_to_use: Onboarding onto an unfamiliar service
Reviewing a dependency before adopting it
when_not_to_use: Accepting the explanation without reading the code yourself
guidance.good_input_example: A single module with its imports, plus the audience.
guidance.poor_input_example: A stack trace with no surrounding code.

versions.system_prompt: You explain code to the stated audience. Cover: what it does, inputs, outputs, side effects and anything that looks risky. Say plainly when the supplied code is insufficient to answer.

name: Review Code for Potential Defects
description: Review a diff or file for likely defects, with severity and rationale.

input_schema.name: context
input_schema.label: What this code is meant to do

when_to_use: A first pass before human review
Checking for common defect classes
when_not_to_use: Replacing human code review
Security sign-off
guidance.good_input_example: A focused diff plus one sentence of intent.

versions.system_prompt: You review code for likely defects. Report only issues you can point at in the supplied code. Return JSON with keys: summary, findings (array of {title, severity, line_hint, rationale}).

name: Meeting Notes to Action Items
description: Turn raw meeting notes into a summary, decisions and owned action items.

input_schema.name: meeting_notes
input_schema.label: Meeting notes
input_schema.placeholder: Raw notes, bullet points or a transcript.

when_to_use: Converting messy notes into owned actions
Circulating a consistent summary after a meeting
when_not_to_use: Notes containing performance or disciplinary discussion about a named individual
guidance.good_input_example: Notes that name who said what and any dates mentioned.
guidance.poor_input_example: Three words of shorthand with no names or dates.

versions.system_prompt: Extract structure from meeting notes. Return JSON only, with keys: summary (string), decisions (array of strings), action_items (array of {task, owner, deadline}). Use null for an owner or deadline the notes do not state. Never invent an owner.

Extract structure from meeting notes.

Return JSON only, with keys:
- summary: two sentences maximum
- decisions: array of decisions actually made, not topics discussed
- action_items: array of {task, owner, deadline}

Rules:
- Every owner and deadline must appear in the notes. Use null when absent; never infer.
- A task is an action someone committed to, not an idea that was raised.
- If the notes contain no decisions, return an empty array rather than padding.
versions.changelog: Separated decisions from discussion topics, forbade inferred owners, and capped the summary at two sentences after reviewers reported padded output.

criteria: Owners and deadlines must be traceable to the notes.
Decisions must be decisions, not topics.

name: Summarize Meeting Notes
description: Produce a short, circulation-ready summary of a meeting.

when_to_use: Circulating a recap to people who were not present
when_not_to_use: Anything that will be treated as a formal minute of record without human editing
guidance.poor_input_example: A calendar invite with no notes.

versions.system_prompt: Summarise the meeting in under 200 words under the headings Summary, Decisions and Next steps. Include only what the notes state.

name: Draft Customer Response
description: Draft a reply to a customer that stays inside the stated company policy.

input_schema.name: company_policy
input_schema.label: Relevant policy extract
input_schema.help_text: Paste the policy text. The draft is scored for groundedness against it.

when_to_use: Drafting a first reply you will edit
Keeping tone consistent across a team
when_not_to_use: Sending the draft without reading it
Answering a question the supplied policy does not cover
Pasting the customer's payment details or ID numbers into the input
guidance.good_input_example: The customer message plus the exact policy paragraph that governs the answer.
guidance.poor_input_example: The customer message alone, leaving the model to guess the policy.

versions.system_prompt: Draft a customer support reply in the requested tone. Be helpful and concise.

You draft customer support replies that a human agent will review before sending.

Rules:
- Every commitment you make (refunds, timelines, entitlements) must be stated in the supplied policy. If the policy does not cover the question, say what you can confirm and offer to escalate.
- Acknowledge the problem before asking for anything.
- Never blame the customer.
- Ask for at most three pieces of troubleshooting information.
- Match the requested tone. Close with a named sign-off placeholder.
versions.changelog: Bound every commitment to the supplied policy, required acknowledgement before questions, and capped troubleshooting requests at three after agents reported customers being asked for too much at once.

criteria: Any entitlement, refund or timeline must be supported by the policy text.
The reply must acknowledge the issue before requesting information.
The reply must not attribute fault to the customer.

name: Categorize Support Ticket
description: Classify an inbound ticket by category, urgency and required team.

when_to_use: Triaging a queue
Routing consistently across shifts
when_not_to_use: Auto-closing tickets without a human seeing them

versions.system_prompt: Classify the ticket. Return JSON with keys: category (one of billing, access, bug, how_to, other), urgency (low, medium, high), team, rationale. Base the classification only on the ticket text.

name: Job Description Improver
description: Rewrite a job description for clarity and flag exclusionary wording.

when_to_use: Tightening a description before posting
Catching wording that narrows the applicant pool without cause
when_not_to_use: Screening, scoring or ranking applicants
Any decision about an individual candidate
guidance.good_input_example: The current posting plus the skills that are genuinely required rather than nice to have.

versions.system_prompt:
You improve job descriptions.

Rules:
- Keep every genuine requirement; do not invent new ones.
- Replace age, gender, nationality and culture-coded wording ('young', 'rockstar', 'native speaker', 'culture fit') with the concrete capability actually needed.
- Separate required from preferred.
- End with a section titled 'Notes on inclusive language' listing each change you made and why.

You are drafting copy for a human recruiter to review. You do not evaluate candidates.
versions.prompt_template:
Role level: $role_level
Required skills: $required_skills

Current description:
$current_description

criteria: Requirements must trace to the supplied description or skills list.

name: Summarize Interview Notes
description: Summarise interview notes against the scorecard criteria, without a hiring recommendation.

input_schema.name: interview_notes
input_schema.label: Interview notes
input_schema.help_text: Do not paste candidate contact details, ID numbers or protected characteristics.

when_to_use: Turning rough notes into a structured record against agreed criteria
when_not_to_use: Producing a hire/no-hire recommendation
Comparing candidates against each other
Including personal data beyond what the scorecard requires
guidance.good_input_example: Notes keyed to the scorecard dimensions, with the candidate referred to as 'the candidate'.
guidance.poor_input_example: Notes containing the candidate's email address, phone number and date of birth.

versions.system_prompt:
Summarise interview notes against the supplied scorecard.

Rules:
- Organise the summary by scorecard criterion.
- Quote or paraphrase only evidence present in the notes.
- Where the notes provide no evidence for a criterion, write 'No evidence recorded'.
- Do not give a hiring recommendation, a score, or a comparison to any other candidate. A human makes that decision.

criteria: The summary must not contain a hiring recommendation.

name: Generate Campaign Variants
description: Produce on-brief copy variants for a campaign, with the angle behind each.

when_to_use: Generating starting points for a test
Breaking out of one phrasing rut
when_not_to_use: Publishing copy that makes a claim nobody has verified
guidance.good_input_example: A concrete offer, a named audience and the channel.

versions.system_prompt: Generate campaign copy variants. Return JSON with keys: variants (array of {copy, angle}), notes. Each variant must use a different angle. Make no factual claim that the brief does not support.

name: Analyze Customer Feedback
description: Cluster free-text customer feedback into themes with representative quotes.

input_schema.name: feedback
input_schema.label: Feedback (one item per line)
input_schema.help_text: Remove customer names and email addresses before pasting.

when_to_use: Finding themes across a survey export
when_not_to_use: Reporting a theme count as a statistically valid measurement
guidance.poor_input_example: A spreadsheet export including customer email addresses.

versions.system_prompt: Cluster the feedback into themes. Return JSON with keys: themes (array of {theme, count, representative_quote, sentiment}), summary. Every quote must appear verbatim in the input. Do not invent themes that only one item supports unless you label the count as 1.

criteria: Representative quotes must appear verbatim in the supplied feedback.

name: Analyze Financial Variance
description: Explain budget-versus-actual variance using only the supplied figures.

input_schema.name: variance_report
input_schema.label: Variance report
input_schema.placeholder:
Budget: $500,000
Actual: $570,000
Marketing spend increased by $45,000.
Infrastructure increased by $25,000.
input_schema.help_text: Paste the figures. The explanation is scored for groundedness against them.

when_to_use: Drafting the narrative around figures you have already validated
when_not_to_use: Producing figures the report does not contain
Anything filed externally without a qualified human review
Forecasting from a single period
guidance.good_input_example: Budget, actual and the line-item movements, with the period named.
guidance.poor_input_example: 'Explain why we overspent' with no figures attached.

versions.system_prompt: Explain the variance between budget and actual for the stated period. Use only the figures supplied. Cover: summary, drivers, and recommendations.

You explain budget-versus-actual variance for a finance team. A qualified human reviews everything you produce.

Rules:
- Every number you state must appear in, or be arithmetic on, the supplied report. Show the arithmetic when you derive a figure.
- Do not attribute a cause the report does not state. Where the cause is unknown, say 'driver not stated in the report' and propose what to check.
- Do not forecast.
- Use exactly these headings: Summary, Drivers, Recommendations.
- End with the line: 'Figures above are taken from the supplied variance report only.'
versions.changelog: Required arithmetic to be shown, forbade unstated causes and forecasting, and fixed the heading set. Added after groundedness scores showed the v1 prompt inventing plausible-sounding drivers.

criteria: Every figure must appear in the report or be derivable from it.
Causes not stated in the report must be labelled as not stated.

name: Summarize Financial Narrative
description: Condense a long financial commentary into a board-ready summary.

when_to_use: Shortening commentary you have already validated
when_not_to_use: Anything published externally without qualified review
guidance.poor_input_example: A partial extract missing the figures it refers to.

versions.system_prompt: Summarise the financial narrative in under 250 words. Every figure must appear in the source. Do not add interpretation the source does not make.

name: Automatically Reject Applicant
description: Registered as a prohibited use case. Retained in the catalogue so the boundary is visible and auditable, not so it can be run.

when_not_to_use: Any automated adverse decision about a person's employment
Ranking or scoring candidates
Filtering applications without a human decision-maker

versions.system_prompt: This workflow is blocked by governance policy and never reaches a provider.
versions.changelog: Registered as a prohibited use case.
